Jīva-gṛbh, ‘seizing alive,’ is, according to Roth, the term for a police official in the Rigveda. But although this sense is rendered possible by the mention of madhyamaśī, perhaps ‘arbitrator,’ in the same passage, it is neither necessary nor probable.
Foot notes St Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.; Siebenzig Lieder, 174.

Jīvant appears to denote a certain plant in one passage of the Atharvaveda, where the edition of Roth and Whitney has the unjustified emendation Jīvala.
Foot notes xix. 39, 3. Cf. Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 960.
With this conjectural form, cf. Jīvalā, an epithet of a plant in Av. vi. 59, 3; viii. 2, 6; 7, 6; xix. 39. 3.

Jīvala Callaki, ‘descendant of Celaka,’ is mentioned in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa as reproving takṣan.
Foot notes ii. 3, 1, 31-35. Cf. Lévi, La Doctrine du Sacrifice, 140.
